title: Reach and use
tagline: how far one can go, and how places are used
summary: How far one can go from any place over the ways drawn there, as a wave of minutes running down the streets; and how a city's walkers share themselves among its places, day by day, against their habit.

layers.title: how far in so many minutes
layers.about: Pick a place on the map: the minutes to every way about it run down the streets as a wave, on foot or by road, at declared speeds. On the ways the world's archives hold for what is in view.

layers.title: where the walkers go, against their habit
layers.about: The Urban Space Usage Index on H3 cells: each cell's share of the day's walkers at the counters, and how far that departs from the same weekday over the twelve weeks before. Follows the clock's date.

source: The ways: Overture Maps and OpenStreetMap. The counts: City of Melbourne's pedestrian counting system. The methods after GOSTnets and eca-resilience, written here (urban-science's access and usage, morphe's shortest paths, physis's H3).
